data.title: Diversified Royalty Corp. Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Diversified Royalty Corp. (TSX: DIV, DIV.DB.A and DIV.DB.B) (the “Corporation” or “DIV”) is pleased to announce its financial results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 (“Q3 2026”) and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

  • Mr. Lube + Tires system sales1 were $126.4 million in Q3, 2026, a 1.7% decrease from $128.5 million in Q3, 2025 (as reported by Mr. Lube Canada LP). Mr. Lube + Tires system sales were $380.5 million* for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a 2.9% increase from $369.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 (as reported by Mr. Lube Canada LP).
  • The weighted average organic royalty growth1 of DIV’s diversified royalty portfolio was 3.6% in Q3 2026 and 3.1% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.6% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 (“Q3 2025”) and 1.0% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The weighted average organic royalty growth1 on a consistent currency basis was 3.0% in Q3 2026 and 3.2% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 0.3% in Q3 2025 and 0.2% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Revenue was $31.5 million in Q3 2026 and $70.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up 72.7% and 36.6%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025.
  • Combined contribution1 was $24.9 million in Q3 2026 and $65.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up 27.2% and 17.5%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025.
  • Distributable cash1 was $15.5 million in Q3 2026 and $40.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up 21.9% and 12.5%, respectively, compared to the same periods in 2025.
  • Payout ratio1 was 86.9% in Q3 2026 based on dividends of $0.0716 per share for the quarter ($0.2850 per share annualized), compared to 91.9% in Q3 2025 based on dividends of $0.0688 per share for the comparable quarter ($0.2750 per share annualized), and 93.3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 based on dividends of $0.2139 per share for the period ($0.2850 per share annualized), compared to 90.6% based on dividends of $0.1938 per share for the comparable 2025 period ($0.2750 per share annualized).
  • On July 6, 2026, DIV closed its previously announced bought deal public offering of 12,339,500 common shares, including 1,609,500 common shares issued pursuant to the full exercise of the over-allotment option, at a price of $4.66 per common share for total gross proceeds of approximately $57.5 million (the “Equity Offering”).
  • On July 7, 2026, DIV used partial net proceeds from the Equity Offering to make a full $38.5 million principal paydown on its Acquisition Facility, reducing the principal balance to nil. DIV had previously drawn on the Acquisition Facility to partially fund the acquisition of the Mr. Lube + Tires franchisor business (the “Acquisition”).

Third Quarter Commentary

Sean Morrison, Chief Executive Officer of DIV, commented: “We are excited to have Mr. Lube + Tires as our first controlled operating franchisor business. This changes DIV’s primary exposure to Mr. Lube + Tires from SSSG, directly impacting the royalty received, to system sales which most impacts adjusted EBITDA. Mr. Lube + Tires’ 1.7% year-over-year decline in system sales for Q3 2026 largely reflects a challenging automotive environment. Inflation in fuel and other vehicle operating costs is leading people to drive fewer kilometres, which has reduced demand for oil changes and maintenance services. Mr. Lube + Tires remains on track to open 18 new locations in 2026 and meet the previously disclosed estimate of $58.7 million in adjusted EBITDA contribution for the twelve months following DIV’s acquisition. Mr. Lube + Tires is budgeting 16 new locations for 2027 and is considering bolt-on acquisition opportunities. Additionally, DIV’s payout ratio has decreased since the acquisition of Mr. Lube + Tires, and we are using our excess cash flow to de-lever Mr. Lube + Tires.”

*System sales reported to DIV by Mr. Lube Canada Limited Partnership (“Mr. Lube LP”) for the period January 1 to June 15, 2026 plus system sales for Mr. Lube + Tires for the period June 16 to September 30, 2026. The royalty arrangements with Mr. Lube LP ceased June 16, 2026 pursuant to the Acquisition. See “Third Party Information” below.

1. In Q3 2026, DIV generated $31.5 million of revenue compared to $18.3 million in Q3 2025. After taking into account the DIV Royalty Entitlement2 (defined below) related to DIV’s royalty arrangements with Nurse Next Door, DIV management fees, and Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA2, DIV’s combined contribution2 was $24.9 million in Q3 2026, compared to $19.6 million in Q3 2025. Combined contribution2 increased primarily due to the incremental Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA2, Mr. Mikes and Oxford’s positive SSSG2, the annual contractual increases at Stratus, Nurse Next Door and BarBurrito, the new fixed higher AIR MILES® royalty effective February 1, 2026, incremental royalty revenue from the 9 new BarBurrito locations added to the BarBurrito royalty pool on March 1, 2026, and the contractual royalty increase from Cheba Hut plus the Incremental Cheba Hut Royalty (defined below), both effective April 1, 2026, partially offset by lower royalty income from Sutton, all as discussed in further detail below.

2. Combined contribution, Mr. Lube + tires adjusted EBITDA and DIV Royalty Entitlement are non-IFRS financial measures and SSSG is a supplementary financial measure – see “Non-IFRS Measures” below.

Franchisor Business Update

Mr. Lube + Tires:

On June 16, 2026, DIV completed the Acquisition of the Mr. Lube + Tires franchisor business. For periods prior to the Acquisition, the contribution of the Mr. Lube + Tires franchisor business to DIV’s combined contribution was generated solely through royalty income and management fees, and following the Acquisition the contribution is generated solely through Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA. More specifically, for the 9 months ended September 30, 2026 the Mr. Lube + Tires franchisor business contributed $15.1 million of royalty income and management fees prior to the Acquisition and $15.6 million of adjusted EBITDA3 after the Acquisition for an aggregate of $30.7 million to DIV’s combined contribution3. This compares to $24.84 million of royalty income and management fees in same prior period under the prior royalty arrangements with Mr. Lube LP, an increase of 23.7%.

After the Acquisition, DIV believes that the system sales of Mr. Lube + Tires is a key measure of the business' contribution, which captures importantly new location growth, of which 9 new locations were added to date, as well as SSSG. This is a change from pre-Acquisition, where SSSG was the key measure of the previous royalty partner performance.

Mr. Lube + Tires franchisor business system sales for Q3, 2026 declined by 1.7% (compared to 16.1% growth in the comparative period in 2025) primarily due to negative 5.1% SSSG3 for Q3 2026, (compared to SSSG3 of 11.2% in the comparative period in 2025), partially offset by system sales growth due to new location openings. The industry is seeing ongoing economic uncertainty, combined with inflationary pressures on gas and other inputs to operate a vehicle. Gasoline prices are up over 20% year-over-year for the past 6 months, impacting share of wallet and overhead to operate a vehicle, which is resulting in fewer kilometers driven (total gasoline volumes have declined year-over-year over this timeframe). These reduced driving patterns are extending service intervals and deferrals. In addition, Mr. Lube + Tires celebrated its 50th anniversary milestone between July 10th and 12th by offering 50% off basic oil changes – although this event was a success from an awareness and celebration point of view, given the incredible volume that weekend, locations focused on basic oil changes and turned away many other services, reducing the average ticket price. Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA3 contribution to DIV is $13.4 million in Q3 2026. There are no comparative period results given the Acquisition closed June 16, 2026. Mr. Lube + Tires business experiences seasonality where Q4 is typically the strongest quarter.

3. Same-store-sales growth or SSSG is a supplementary financial measures and combined contribution and Mr. Lube + tires adjusted EBITDA are non-IFRS financial measures – see “Non-IFRS Measures” below.

Royalty Partner Business Updates

Stratus: Royalty income from SBS Franchising LLC (“Stratus”) was $2.4 million (US$1.7 million translated at an average foreign exchange rate of $1.3995 to US$1.00) for Q3 2026. The fixed royalty payable by Stratus increases each November at a rate of 5% until and including November 2026 and 4% each November thereafter during the term of the license, with the most recent increase effective November 15, 2025.

Nurse Next Door: The royalty entitlement to DIV (the “DIV Royalty Entitlement4”) from Nurse Next Door Professional Homecare Services Inc. (“Nurse Next Door”) was $1.4 million in Q3 2026. The DIV Royalty Entitlement from Nurse Next Door grows at a fixed rate of 2.0% per annum during the term of the license, with the most recent increase effective October 1, 2025.

4. DIV Royalty Entitlement is a non-IFRS measure – see “Non-IFRS Measures” below.

Mr. Mikes: SSSG5 for Mr. Mikes Restaurants Corporation (“Mr. Mikes”) restaurants in the Mr. Mikes royalty pool was 4.7% in Q3 2026, compared to SSSG of 1.0% in Q3 2025. The royalty income from Mr. Mikes was $1.1 million for both Q3 2026 and Q3 2025, respectively. The Q3 2026 results were slightly higher due to increased SSSG, partially offset by the two store closures in the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026.

5. Same-store-sales growth or SSSG is a supplementary financial measure – see “Non-IFRS Measures” below.

Oxford: The Oxford Learning Centres, Inc. (“Oxford”) locations in the Oxford royalty pool generated SSSG6 (on a constant currency basis) of 1.5% in Q3 2026 (after the impact of foreign currency translation, SSSG was 1.7%), compared to SSSG of 4.4% in Q3 2025 (on a constant currency basis). The royalty income from Oxford was $1.1 million for both Q3 2026 and Q3 2025, respectively.

6. Same-store-sales growth or SSSG is a supplementary financial measure – see “Non-IFRS Measures” below.

AIR MILES®: In Q3 2026, royalty income of $1.0 million was generated from the AIR MILES® Licenses compared to $0.8 million generated in Q3 2025, an increase of 20%. The increase is largely due to the AIR MILES Amendment effective February 1, 2026, compared to royalty income based on gross billings for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Sutton: On September 1, 2026, the Company and SGRS LP amended the royalty arrangement with Sutton to replace the prior fixed royalty payments based on the number of agents in a royalty pool with variable royalty payments retroactively effective to May 1, 2026. Under the variable royalty arrangements, Sutton now pays SGRS LP a variable royalty based on a baseline amount per month, which baseline amount increases or decreases each month depending on amounts collected by Sutton from its franchisees in the prior month (the “Sutton Variable Royalty”).

The continued weakness in the Canadian housing market has resulted in a further reduction in royalty payments from Sutton in accordance with the terms of the Sutton Variable Royalty and impacted the timing of the receipt of certain royalty payments from Sutton. As a result, DIV recorded a further $4.7 million impairment for the three months ended September 30, 2026 to intangible assets related to SGRS Rights. In addition, on September 1, 2026 and September 23, 2026, respectively, SGRS LP made $1.3 million and $0.5 million principal payments, respectively, on the SGRS LP term loan.

In Q3 2026, royalty income was $0.5 million which reflects the Sutton Variable Royalty effective May 1, 2026, compared to $0.8 million in Q3 2025, which reflects the prior contractual fixed royalty net of 33% royalty relief in the comparable period.

BarBurrito: Royalty income from BarBurrito Restaurants Inc. (“BarBurrito”) was $2.3 million for Q3 2026. The royalty payable by BarBurrito initially grows at a fixed rate of 4% per annum each March up to and including March 2030 and, commencing on January 1, 2031, will fluctuate based on the gross sales of the BarBurrito locations in the royalty pool.

On March 1, 2026, the BarBurrito royalty pool was adjusted to add nine eligible BarBurrito restaurants to the BarBurrito royalty pool, which resulted in an increase of $32,708 ($392,496 annualized) to the monthly royalty payment payable by BarBurrito to DIV effective March 1, 2026.

Cheba Hut: Royalty income from Cheba Hut Franchising, Inc. (“Cheba Hut”) was $1.8 million for Q3 2026 (US$1.3 million translated at an average foreign exchange rate of 1.3995 to US$1.00). The fixed royalty payable by Cheba Hut increases each April at a rate equal to the greater of 3.5% and the U.S. Consumer Price Index (“U.S. CPI”) plus 1.5%.

On April 1, 2026, DIV purchased a US$0.9 million annualized incremental royalty from Cheba Hut for US$7.2 million (the “Incremental Cheba Hut Royalty”). The Incremental Cheba Hut Royalty is effective April 1, 2026.

Distributable Cash and Dividends Declared

In Q3 2026, distributable cash7 increased to $15.5 million ($0.0824 per share), compared to $12.7 million ($0.0748 per share), in Q3 2025. The increase in increase distributable cash per share7 for the quarter was primarily due to an increase in distributable cash, partially offset by a higher weighted average number of common shares outstanding. The increase in distributable cash was primarily due to incremental Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA7, partially offset by higher interest expense, professional fees, general and administrative expenses, and salaries and benefits.

In Q3 2026, the payout ratio7 was 86.9% on dividends of $0.0716 per share, compared to the payout ratio of 91.9% on dividends of $0.0688 per share for the same respective period in 2025. The lower payout ratio was primarily due to higher distributable cash per share partially offset by higher dividends declared per share.

7. Distributable cash and Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA are non-IFRS financial measures and distributable cash per share and payout ratio are non-IFRS ratios – see “Non-IFRS Measures” below.

Net Income

Net income for Q3 2026 was $5.5 million compared to net income of $8.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in net income in Q3 2026 was primarily due to the higher general and administrative expenses, interest expenses, salaries expense, impairment loss on the SGRS Rights (summarized above) and AIR MILES Rights due to the 10-year, fixed royalty payment period of the AIR MILES Amendment, partially offset by the higher adjusted combined contribution8, fair value adjustments on financial instruments and lower other finance costs.

8. Combined contribution is a non-IFRS financial measure – see “Non-IFRS Measures” below.

About Diversified Royalty Corp.

DIV is a multi-royalty corporation, engaged in the business of acquiring top-line royalties from well-managed multi-location businesses and franchisors in North America. DIV’s objective is to acquire predictable, growing royalty streams from a diverse group of multi-location businesses and franchisors. DIV, through its subsidiary, Mr. Lube Canada Ltd., also operates the Mr. Lube + Tires franchisor business in Canada. Mr. Lube + Tires is the leading Canadian automotive service chain specializing in fast, drive-in and drive-through, no-appointment-needed vehicle maintenance.

DIV currently owns the Sutton, Mr. Mikes, Nurse Next Door, Oxford Learning Centres, Stratus Building Solutions, BarBurrito, Cheba Hut and AIR MILES® trademarks. Sutton is among the leading residential real estate brokerage franchisor businesses in Canada. Mr. Mikes operates casual steakhouse restaurants primarily in western Canadian communities. Nurse Next Door is a home care provider with locations across Canada and the United States as well as in Australia. Oxford Learning Centres is one of Canada’s leading franchisee supplemental education services. Stratus Building Solutions is a leading commercial cleaning service franchise company providing comprehensive janitorial, building cleaning, and office cleaning services primarily in the United States. BarBurrito is the largest quick service Mexican restaurant food chain in Canada. Cheba Hut is a fast casual toasted sub sandwich franchise with locations in the United States. AIR MILES® was a Canadian loyalty program.

DIV’s objective is to increase cash flow per share by making accretive royalty purchases and through the growth of purchased royalties and the Mr. Lube + Tires franchisor business. DIV intends to continue to pay a predictable and stable monthly dividend to shareholders and increase the dividend over time, in each case as cash flow per share allows.

Non-IFRS Measures

Management believes that disclosing certain non-IFRS financial measures, non-IFRS ratios and supplementary financial measures provides readers with important information regarding the Corporation’s financial performance and its ability to pay dividends and the performance of its royalty partners and of Mr. Lube + Tires. By considering these measures in combination with the most closely comparable IFRS measure, management believes that investors are provided with additional and more useful information about the Corporation, its royalty partners and Mr. Lube + Tires than investors would have if they simply considered IFRS measures alone. The non-IFRS financial measures, non-IFRS ratios and supplementary financial measures do not have standardized meanings prescribed by IFRS and therefore are unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other issuers. Investors are cautioned that non-IFRS measures should not be construed as a substitute or an alternative to net income or cash flows from operating activities as determined in accordance with IFRS.

“Adjusted royalty income”, “adjusted royalty partner revenue”, “combined contribution”, “Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA”, “DIV Royalty Entitlement” and “distributable cash” are used as non-IFRS financial measures in this news release.

Adjusted royalty income is calculated as royalty income from DIV’s royalty partners, plus the DIV Royalty Entitlement received by NND Royalties LP from Nurse Next Door. Adjusted royalty partner revenue is calculated as adjusted royalty income plus management fees received from Royalty Partners. Combined contribution is calculated as adjusted royalty partner revenue plus adjusted Mr. Lube + Tires EBITDA. Management believes that distributable cash provides investors with useful information about the amount of cash the Corporation has generated to cover dividends on its common shares during the applicable period. Readers should be cautioned, however, that distributable cash should not be construed as an alternative to the statement of cash flows as a measure of liquidity and cash flows of the Corporation. The Corporation’s method of calculating distributable cash may differ from that of other issuers and companies and, accordingly, distributable cash may not be comparable to similar measures used by other issuers or companies. Distributable cash was previously calculated in Q3 2025 as Normalized EBITDA less interest expense on the credit facilities, less distributions on exchangeable partnership units, less net current income tax expense (after foreign tax credit on US withholding taxes paid), plus interest income. The calculation has been revised as management believes the updated calculation provides a more representative view of the distributable cash generated by DIV. data.title: Noel Tata appointed Voltas Chairman Emeritus; Sunil D’Souza to take over as Chairman
data.description:
Noel N Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, has been appointed as Chairman Emeritus of Voltas, a day after he retired as Chairman and Director of the leading cooling products maker.

Noel Tata will retire as Chairman and Director of Voltas Ltd on November 11, 2026, upon attaining the age of superannuation under Tata Group governance guidelines.

Following his retirement, “the Board has appointed him as Chairman Emeritus of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026,” said Voltas, a Tata Group firm, in its regulatory filing.

Noel Tata to become Chairman Emeritus

The Companies Act 2013 mandates that any managing director or whole-time director cannot be appointed or continue employment if they are 70 years of age or older.

Noel Tata, who was born on November 12, 1956, will turn 70 on November 12, 2026. He has been associated with Voltas since 2003.

Additionally, the board has appointed Sunil D’Souza as the new Chairman of Voltas.

D’Souza currently leads the Tata Group’s FMCG arm, Tata Consumer Products Ltd (TCPL), as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. The company sells a wide range of consumer products, including salt, tea, coffee, packaged foods and beverages under brands such as Tata Salt, Tata Tea, Tetley and Tata Sampann.

“The Board has appointed Sunil Alaric D’Souza as Chairman of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026,” Voltas said.

Sunil D’Souza appointed Voltas Chairman

Moreover, the tenure of Voltas Managing Director C P Mukundan Menon will end on May 24, 2027, when he will retire from the company’s services in line with the Tata Group’s retirement policy for executive directors.

The board has approved the appointment of Jayant Balan, currently Head of the Room Air Conditioner Business, as an Additional Director and Managing Director for a five-year term beginning May 25, 2027, subject to shareholders’ approval.

“As part of a planned succession process, the Board, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, has approved the appointment of Jayant Balan, currently Head - Room Air Conditioner Business, as an Additional Director and Managing Director of the Company for a term of five years commencing from May 25, 2027,” Voltas said.

This will be subject to the approval of the shareholders.

Jayant Balan named Managing Director-designate

To ensure a smooth transition, Balan has been redesignated as Head – Room Air Conditioner Business and Managing Director Designate until his appointment takes effect.

The board has also approved the appointment of Venkatesalu Palaniswamy as an Additional Director in the non-independent, non-executive category with effect from November 12, 2026.
